summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease Hb-SS, a history of avascular necrosis, and prior osteosarcoma was admitted for a sickle cell pain crisis triggered by dehydration from antibiotic-associated diarrhea. She presented with abdominal pain, watery diarrhea, and back and extremity pain. A recent ER diagnosis of proctitis had led to treatment with Cipro and Flagyl, but GI consultation concluded the diarrhea and bright red blood per rectum were likely adverse effects of the antibiotics. The antibiotics were discontinued, symptoms resolved, and she was managed with IV fluids, a Dilaudid PCA tapered to oral analgesics, and hydroxyurea. Her hemoglobin declined slightly but remained stable without transfusion. Hypomagnesemia was corrected with supplementation. She improved clinically, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with instructions to continue medications, monitor for recurrent symptoms, and follow up with hematology, orthopedics, and primary care for ongoing management.
